stories.title: Ken Griffin Seals $3.3B Construction Loan for Manhattan Office Tower
stories.excerpt: Billionaire money manager Ken Griffin now has a firm financial investment in Midtown Manhattan months after a public feud with New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani. Griffin, as part of a joint venture with Vornado Realty Trust and Rudin, has landed $3.3 billion of construction financing to develop a 66-story office tower at 350 Park Avenue, the sponsorship announced Wednesday. A lending syndicate led by Wells Fargo and J.P. Morgan Chase originated the loan for the 1.9 million-square-foot building. Griffin will have a 60 percent stake in 350 Park Avenue under the newly formed JV with Vornado holding 36 percent and Rudin 4 percent, the companies also announced. Griffin’s Citadel financial firm will lease 1.05 million square feet in the new office tower, which is slated for completion in 2032. The remaining 850,000 square feet on the building’s upper floors will be marketed to other tenants, according to the New York Post, which first reported the loan. The 350 Park deal closed on the heels of Mamdani posting a social media video in April touting a tax on pieds-à-terre in front of Griffin’s penthouse at 220 Central Park South. The move sparked sharp criticism of Mamdani from leading figures in the commercial real estate industry, including Vornado CEO Steven Roth during his first-quarter earnings call in early May. Wells Fargo and J.P. Morgan did not immediately return requests for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Ken Griffin (Citadel), Vornado, Rudin close $3.3B construction loan for 350 Park Avenue office tower.
Griffin's Citadel leases 1.05M of 1.9M sf; completion 2032; Wells Fargo and JPMorgan lead syndicate.
Signals major capital commitment to Midtown Manhattan office despite recent public feud with NYC Mayor.
stories.summary: Citadel CEO Ken Griffin, through a joint venture with Vornado Realty Trust (36%) and Rudin (4%), has secured $3.3 billion in construction financing for a 66-story, 1.9 million-square-foot office tower at 350 Park Avenue in Midtown Manhattan. Griffin controls 60% of the deal and his firm will anchor 1.05 million square feet, with the building targeting completion in 2032. Wells Fargo and JPMorgan Chase led the lending syndicate.
stories.impact: Demonstrates renewed institutional capital appetite for large-scale office development in Manhattan's prime submarket despite structural office headwinds. Griffin's anchor tenancy reduces leasing risk on ~850K sf of speculative space, signaling his confidence in mid-2030s office demand recovery in Midtown—likely contingent on AI/finance sector consolidation and return-to-office trends.

stories.title: Lurie Advances Plan for Freedom West 2.0; Would Bring 2,400 Apartments to Western Addition
stories.excerpt: San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie on Wednesday introduced legislation to advance Freedom West 2.0, a long-planned project in the Western Addition neighborhood that could bring nearly 2,400 new homes to the neighborhood, with more than 17% expected to be affordable. The first phase will deliver 115 units of affordable senior housing and a rebuilt Freedom West Cooperative, with groundbreaking anticipated in the first half of 2027. The full plan envisions four city blocks with a mix of market-rate and affordable housing, public open space and an innovation center. “Residents of Freedom West and this community have long advocated for this vision, and today, we are moving to make it a reality,” said Lurie. “This investment in the future of the Western Addition helps secure a stronger future for our entire city.” To strengthen the co-op’s long-term financial stability, Freedom West 2.0 will generate revenue through ground leases with affordable housing developers, retail spaces in the new buildings and profit-sharing from future market-rate development. The post Lurie Advances Plan for Freedom West 2.0; Would Bring 2,400 Apartments to Western Addition appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: SF Mayor Lurie advances Freedom West 2.0: 2,400 new homes, 17%+ affordable, Western Addition neighborhood.
Phase 1 groundbreaking H1 2027; 115 senior affordable units and rebuilt cooperative lead the project.
Mixed-income development model: ground leases, retail, profit-sharing fund long-term co-op financial stability.
stories.summary: San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie introduced legislation to advance Freedom West 2.0, a phased mixed-income development in the Western Addition that will deliver approximately 2,400 homes with more than 17% designated as affordable. Phase 1, with groundbreaking expected in the first half of 2027, includes 115 affordable senior units and a rebuilt Freedom West Cooperative. The full project spans four city blocks with market-rate and affordable housing, public open space, and an innovation center, funded through ground leases, retail operations, and profit-sharing from market-rate development.
stories.impact: Signals SF's pivot toward hybrid subsidy models to unlock large-scale development in constrained urban neighborhoods. For multifamily developers, the profit-sharing mechanism and ground-lease revenue streams reduce reliance on upfront public funding, creating a replicable playbook for affordable-heavy projects in Bay Area submarkets. Groundbreaking in H1 2027 anchors Western Addition absorption demand for the next decade.

stories.title: Canadian Investor Buys Two Hotels in Palm Beach County for More Than $48M
stories.excerpt: Brasswater paid more than $48 million to buy two Hampton Inns hotels in Palm Beach County, Fla., from Hospitality Investors Trust, property records show. In the biggest transaction, the Montrael-based firm paid at least $29 million for the 164-room Hampton Inn & Suites Boynton Beach. The 102,476-square-foot property was built in 1997 on a 3-acre property at 1475 Gateway Boulevard, about a mile west of Interstate 95. Secondly, Brasswater bought the 110-room Hampton Inn West Palm Beach Florida Turnpike for more than $19 million. The 68,800-square-foot asset sits just west of Florida Turnpike, adjacent to Okeechobee Boulevard at 2025 Vista Parkway. It was built on a 2.4-acre site in 2001. The total of the recent purchases is likely higher to include the furniture and business operations of the Hilton properties, which is often not reflected in public deeds that only value the real estate. New York-based Axonic Capital supplied a debt package backing both hotels totaling $42.2 million. Fairfax, Va.-based Hospitality Investors Trust had purchased the two hotels for a combined $43.6 million in 2015. The recent sales come as Hospitality Investors Trust has been selling off some of its South Florida properties. Starting in June, it sold a 117-room Hampton Inn in Palm Beach Gardens for $14.3 million, followed by the $9.8 million sale of another 106-room Hampton Inn in Deerfield Beach. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Canadian investor Brasswater acquires two Hampton Inns in Palm Beach County for $48M+ (160-room, 110-room properties).
Axonic Capital provides $42.2M debt package; Hospitality Investors Trust divests at modest loss after 2023 purchase.
Asset sales suggest investor repositioning in Florida hospitality; limited direct multifamily signal.
stories.summary: Montreal-based Brasswater purchased two Hampton Inn properties in Palm Beach County, Florida, for more than $48 million total: a 164-room property in Boynton Beach for $29 million and a 110-room property near West Palm Beach for $19 million. The transaction was funded by a $42.2 million debt package from New York-based Axonic Capital. The seller, Hospitality Investors Trust, appears to have divested at a loss relative to its 2023 acquisition price of $43.6 million combined.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. Reflects hospitality investor rotation and modest debt availability for non-core asset classes. The modest loss on sale may indicate softening Palm Beach hotel fundamentals, which could signal competitive market conditions for future multifamily absorption in coastal South Florida submarkets if leisure/tourism demand wavers.

stories.title: Mexican Eatery Casa Carmen to Open Third Manhattan Location
stories.excerpt: Mexican restaurant Casa Carmen is opening its third Manhattan location in Midtown East, Commercial Observer has learned. The restaurant concept started by chef Carmen “Titita” Ramírez Degollado signed a 15-year, 6,917-square-foot lease to serve up traditional Mexican cuisine at Sage’s 437 Madison Avenue, according to tenant broker Retail by MONA as well as the landlord. Asking rent for the space was $200 per square foot, according to Retail by MONA. “Casa Carmen is a natural fit for 437 Madison Avenue and our hospitality-driven approach to the workplace,” Michael Lenchner, director of leasing at Sage, said in a statement. “We are continually looking for ways to make the workplace experience more convenient, engaging and enjoyable for our tenants and their employees. Bringing a restaurant of Casa Carmen’s caliber into the building gives our members and tenants another exceptional option right outside their office doors.” CBRE’s Matthew Chmielecki and Preston Cannon negotiated on behalf of the landlord, while John DiGangi of Retail by MONA represented Casa Carmen in the deal. CBRE did not immediately respond to a request for comment. “Midtown is seeing a new wave of investment and energy, driven by major corporate headquarters, office activity and the continued evolution of the neighborhood,” Brandon Singer, founder and CEO of Retail by MONA, said in a statement. “As more companies make significant commitments to the area, we’re seeing opportunities for restaurant and hospitality concepts that can serve the growing demand from office workers, residents and visitors alike.” The New York Post briefly mentioned the deal in an Oct. 11 writeup but provided no details. Casa Carmen has existing locations at 114 Franklin Street in Tribeca and 5 West 21st Street in the Flatiron District. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Mexican restaurant Casa Carmen signs 15-year lease at 437 Madison Avenue, Midtown East Manhattan.
6,917-sf space at $200/sf ($1.38M annualized rent); tenant relocates from 240 Madison Avenue.
Restaurant backfill signals office landlord tenant-mix diversification; limited direct multifamily relevance.
stories.summary: Chef Carmen "Titita" Ramírez Degollado's Mexican restaurant Casa Carmen signed a 15-year lease for 6,917 square feet at 437 Madison Avenue in Midtown East at an asking rent of $200 per square foot. The concept is opening its third Manhattan location and will relocate from 240 Madison Avenue, using the space for executive offices, design, and a showroom. Landlord Sage positioned the restaurant as part of a hospitality-driven workplace strategy to enhance tenant amenities.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to multifamily development. Signals office landlords are investing in F&B and amenity density to retain and attract office tenants amid structural demand softness—a tactic unlikely to move needles on occupied office stock, but does indicate landlords' willingness to co-tenant retail to reduce vacancy risk in Midtown East.

stories.title: L.A. Multifamily Sales Jump 44%
stories.excerpt: Los Angeles County multifamily investment sales are up after the third quarter while average rent and occupancy rates appear to be stuck in neutral. Sales volume for multifamily properties with 50 or more units reached $3.3 billion so far on the year, up 44 percent from the same period in 2025, while the average sale price declined to $357,085 per unit, according to a new Colliers market report. At the same time, L.A.’s apartment occupancy rate held at 94.1 percent in the third quarter, unchanged from the previous quarter, and down only slightly from 94.4 percent a year earlier. Average monthly effective rent increased by $6 to $2,428 per unit in the third quarter, but it is back to the same rate after the third quarter of 2025. Colliers pinned both the annual decline in occupancy and the static rent in part to new construction. Colliers estimates developers added 4,277 units during the third quarter, which is about 72 percent more than in the second quarter. Absorption of these units totaled 3,809 units, up significantly from 2,429 the previous quarter and 2,360 a year ago. However, the apartment construction pipeline is shrinking. There were 23,426 units under construction at the end of the third quarter, down from 24,877 in the second quarter and 25,421 a year earlier. L.A. County has completed more than 58,800 apartments since the second quarter of 2021, per Colliers. The Westside remained the most expensive area, with average effective rents at $3,336 per month, despite occupancy of 92.9 percent. The submarket also had the largest development pipeline with 5,894 units under construction. The Hollywood and Mid-Wilshire neighborhoods recorded an average rent of $2,355 and occupancy of 92 percent, the second-lowest occupancy rate for the top submarkets. It also led the region in new deliveries with 1,869 units added during the quarter, while 5,113 units are under construction. Downtown and the areas going into Central L.A. posted the market’s lowest occupancy rate
bullets: LA County multifamily sales up 44% YTD to $3.3B; average price $357K/unit; occupancy flat at 94.1%.
Q3 2026: 4,277 new units added (72% above Q2), absorbed 3,809 units; rents +$6 to $2,428/month.
New supply and absorb rising, but rent growth stalled YoY; oversupply risk emerging in LA market.
stories.summary: Los Angeles County multifamily investment sales reached $3.3 billion year-to-date through Q3 2026, up 44% from the same period in 2025, though average per-unit sale price declined to $357,085. Occupancy remained flat at 94.1% in Q3, unchanged from Q2 and down only slightly from 94.4% a year prior. Average effective monthly rent increased just $6 to $2,428 per unit in Q3 and has returned to Q3 2025 levels, with Colliers attributing the rent stagnation and occupancy decline partly to robust new construction: developers delivered 4,277 units in Q3 (72% above Q2) with absorption of 3,809 units.
stories.impact: Los Angeles multifamily market is transitioning from supply constraint to absorption pressure. The 44% surge in sales volume alongside flat rents and declining occupancy suggests investor confidence is weakening—lower cap rates on sales mask underlying demand softness. The 4,277-unit Q3 delivery and rising absorb indicate a pipeline inflection point; developers should monitor Q4 2026–Q1 2027 deliveries closely. Rent growth stalling at $2,428/month in one of the nation's priciest metros signals limited pricing power and increased competition for middle-market tenants, particularly in secondary submarkets.

stories.title: BGO Acquires Newly Built Industrial from Bluewater, Affinius
stories.excerpt: BGO acquired 545 Washington St., a newly constructed, 132,055-square-foot Class A industrial property in Wrentham, MA, for a reported $34.9 million on behalf of an institutional investor. Completed in 2023, the property is 100% leased to two tenants. JLL Capital Markets senior managing directors Michael Restivo and John Plower, along with senior director David Coffman and director Tommy Hovey represented the seller, Bluewater Property Group and Affinius Capital. Senior managing director Joe Fabiano from JLL’s Leasing Advisory team also assisted in the sale. “545 Washington St. combines several of the characteristics we continue to value in industrial real estate: modern specifications, strong tenancy, and connectivity to major population and distribution networks,” said Steve Lekki, managing director, BGO. “We believe the property is well positioned to serve the evolving needs of logistics and distribution users across New England, and we are pleased to make this investment on behalf of our client.” The post BGO Acquires Newly Built Industrial from Bluewater, Affinius appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: BGO acquires 545 Washington St., 132K-sf Class A industrial in Wrentham, MA for $34.9M on behalf of institutional investor.
Built 2023, 100% leased to two tenants; strong New England logistics connectivity position.
Industrial market fundamentals remain solid; valuations support institutional capital deployment in supply-constrained Northeast.
stories.summary: BGO acquired 545 Washington Street, a 132,055-square-foot newly constructed Class A industrial property in Wrentham, Massachusetts, for $34.9 million on behalf of an institutional investor. Completed in 2023, the property is fully leased to two tenants and is positioned in an established industrial park with strong connectivity to major population and distribution networks. JLL Capital Markets represented the sellers, Bluewater Property Group and Affinius Capital.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. Reflects continued institutional capital appetite for modern, fully-leased industrial assets in supply-constrained Northeast submarkets. Wrentham's proximity to Boston and distribution networks makes it a proxy for supply-chain real estate demand resilience, but does not signal shifts in residential demand or development feasibility in the region.

stories.title: Designer Indecor Home Inks 17K-SF Lease at GFP’s 247 West 37th Street
stories.excerpt: Home is where the decor is. Indecor Home, a designer and manufacturer of bath accessories, shower curtains, rugs and other textiles, has taken 16,806 square feet of office and showroom space across the entire fifth floor of GFP Real Estate’s 247 West 37th Street in Manhattan’s Garment District, the landlord announced Wednesday. The tenant will relocate from 240 Madison Avenue and use its new space as executive, sales and design offices, as well as a home products showroom. The length of the lease was 10 years. The asking rent was not disclosed, but the average asking rent for office space in Midtown Manhattan was $85.08 per square foot during the third quarter of 2026, according to Colliers data. “Indecor needed room to bring its teams and showroom together, and the full floor at 247 West 37th Street gives it the flexibility to do that,” GFP’s Matthew Mandell, who represented the landlord on this deal, said in a statement. “The building continues to attract businesses that value a central Manhattan location and space they can shape around the way they work.” Indecor Home was represented by David Menaged from Intrepid Real Estate Group. Menaged did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Built in 1924, 247 West 37th Street is a 19-story, 271,000-square-foot office property. Other tenants in the building include security services firm Heightened Security, knitwear manufacturer Knit Illustrated and apparel maker AJC Trading. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Indecor Home leases 16.8K-sf full fifth floor at 247 West 37th Street, Manhattan Garment District, 10-year term.
Tenant relocates from 240 Madison Avenue to expand office, design, and showroom operations; asking rent not disclosed.
Mid-market office leasing activity in Garment District signals selective Manhattan office demand; limited multifamily relevance.
stories.summary: Indecor Home, a designer and manufacturer of bath accessories and textiles, leased the entire fifth floor (16,806 square feet) at GFP Real Estate's 247 West 37th Street in Manhattan's Garment District under a 10-year lease. The tenant will relocate from 240 Madison Avenue and use the space for executive and sales offices, design operations, and a home products showroom. The asking rent was not disclosed, though Midtown Manhattan office space averaged $85.08 per square foot in Q3 2026.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to multifamily development. Signals modest office leasing activity and tenant consolidation in Manhattan's secondary submarkets (Garment District). The relocation from 240 Madison Avenue to a larger floorplate may indicate landlord pressure or tenant desire for amenity-rich, full-floor spaces—a trend that could eventually push marginal office tenants to relocate to secondary markets, freeing office supply for future residential conversion, but this effect remains distant.

stories.title: Colliers to Auction 30K-SF Flex Building in Allentown
stories.excerpt: Colliers announced the auction of 954 Marcon Boulevard, a vacant flex building in Allentown, Lehigh County, Pennsylvania. The 30,100-square-foot property sits on 3.44 acres within an established industrial park.Colliers Vice Chair Jacklene Chesler, Senior Vice President Patrick Norris and Transaction Manager Brittany Leventoff are exclusively marketing the offering in partnership with Ten-X. The building features 18- to 22-foot clear heights, two existing loading docks, and 2,500-amp three-phase power. Conceptual plans contemplate converting the building into a flex facility with four loading docks, a configuration aligned with demand from distribution, manufacturing, assembly, technology, life sciences and service-oriented users.Strategically positioned in the Lehigh Valley industrial corridor, the property is surrounded by several existing flex and industrial properties. The site is also less than one mile from Lehigh Valley International Airport, a major distribution hub for FedEx. “Vacant, well-located flex product is increasingly difficult to find in the Lehigh Valley,” said Jacklene Chesler, Vice Chair at Colliers. The post Colliers to Auction 30K-SF Flex Building in Allentown appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Colliers to auction 954 Marcon Boulevard, 30.1K-sf vacant flex building in Allentown industrial park, Lehigh County, PA.
3.44-acre site with 18-22 ft ceilings, two docks, heavy power; conceptual flex conversion plans included.
Allentown flex industrial asset; auction format suggests motivated seller or challenging leasing environment.
stories.summary: Colliers announced the auction of 954 Marcon Boulevard, a 30,100-square-foot vacant flex building in Allentown, Pennsylvania, situated on 3.44 acres in an established industrial park. The property features 18- to 22-foot clear heights, two loading docks, and 2,500-amp three-phase power, with conceptual plans for conversion into a four-unit flex facility. Colliers Vice Chair Jacklene Chesler and team are marketing the offering in partnership with Ten-X.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. Allentown's industrial market is peripheral to major multifamily metros; the auction format suggests either distressed positioning or soft regional industrial demand. If Lehigh Valley industrial market is softening, it could signal broader secondary-market absorption challenges and reduced investor appetite for tertiary real estate across asset classes.

stories.title: Federal Realty Investment Trust Announces Nine New Retail Tenants at Virginia Gateway
stories.excerpt: Federal Realty Investment Trust announced nine new merchants at Virginia Gateway, building on a year of strong leasing activity that has already brought eight new businesses to the Gainesville shopping center. The latest additions span restaurants, specialty retail, fitness and personal care. “The caliber and diversity of businesses choosing Virginia Gateway speaks to the strength of the center and its continued appeal to leading retail and restaurant operators,” said Mike Ennes, Senior Vice President of Asset Management at Federal Realty. “Adding nine new merchants on the heels of eight openings this year is a significant reflection of Virginia Gateway’s established position in the market.” The merchants expected to open this year include Frye’s Famous Crab Cakes, Talkin’ Tacos, and LaserAway. Additional merchants scheduled to open in early 2027 include The Baked Bear, Dumont Creamery & Cafe, Ignite + Immerse, Orangetheory Fitness, MINISO, and Paris Baguette. Virginia Gateway has welcomed eight new merchants since March. The post Federal Realty Investment Trust Announces Nine New Retail Tenants at Virginia Gateway appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Federal Realty announces nine new tenants at Virginia Gateway shopping center (Gainesville), complementing eight 2026 openings.
Tenants span restaurants (Frye's Crab Cakes, Talkin' Tacos, LaserAway, Orangetheory), specialty retail (MINISO, Paris Baguette).
Strong retail leasing velocity signals robust local demand and mixed-use anchor power in Gainesville submarket.
stories.summary: Federal Realty Investment Trust announced nine new merchants coming to Virginia Gateway shopping center in Gainesville, following eight merchant openings earlier in 2026. The latest additions span restaurants (Frye's Famous Crab Cakes, Talkin' Tacos, The Baked Bear, Dumont Creamery & Cafe), specialty retail (MINISO, Paris Baguette), fitness (Orangetheory, Ignite + Immerse), and personal services (LaserAway). Most are scheduled to open in early 2027.
stories.impact: Gainesville's retail leasing momentum at Virginia Gateway signals strong local consumer demand and neighborhood economic vitality, which supports indirect multifamily development thesis in the Gainesville metro. High-velocity retail leasing typically precedes or accompanies residential in-migration and rent growth; developers should monitor Gainesville's job growth (particularly in education, healthcare, tech) to assess future multifamily absorption potential in trade areas surrounding Virginia Gateway.

stories.title: Wayfair Unveils Launch Date for Denver Store
stories.excerpt: The retailer was known solely for its online offerings, but has decided to build warehouses for walk-in customers. The popular furniture retailer Wayfair is preparing to open a new store in Denver and says the grand opening is scheduled for next month. The store will occupy the former Macy’s at 8298 E. Northfield Blvd., which closed last year. It’s Wayfair’s first store in the Mountain West region. This will be the company’s fourth large-format store, covering approximately 140,000 square feet. The two-story store will feature 19 departments, including furniture, housewares, appliances, mattresses, florals, decor and dedicated areas for design services. The store will be situated in the Avenues at Northfield, a Stockdale Capital Partners-owned center. The company, which acquired the center in 2022, is planning to add a 103,000-square-foot Life Time facility, a national grocery store and housing. The post Wayfair Unveils Launch Date for Denver Store appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Wayfair to open fourth large-format store in Denver; 140K-sf two-story at former Macy's, 8298 E. Northfield Blvd.
Grand opening scheduled next month; first Mountain West location; includes 19 departments, design services.
Retail expansion signals demand for experiential furniture shopping; modest demographic/demand signal for Denver metro.
stories.summary: Wayfair announced a January 2027 grand opening for its fourth large-format store in Denver, occupying the former Macy's at 8298 East Northfield Boulevard in the Avenues at Northfield shopping center (owned by Stockdale Capital Partners). The 140,000-square-foot, two-story location will be Wayfair's first in the Mountain West region and will feature 19 departments including furniture, housewares, appliances, mattresses, and design services. The center is also planning a 103,000-square-foot Life Time facility, national grocery anchor, and new housing.
stories.impact: Wayfair's Denver expansion and associated Life Time fitness + mixed-use development at Avenues at Northfield signals investor confidence in Denver metro's retail and residential demand. The shift from online-only to experiential retail format, combined with multifamily plans at the center, indicates recognition of suburban Denver's in-migration momentum and lifestyle amenity clustering. For multifamily developers, this signals potential for transit-adjacent or mixed-use developments near high-traffic retail nodes in Denver's metro expansion zones.
